decision_table.name: Determine_NH_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file New Hampshire Business Profits Tax (BPT) return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus ($109,000 gross income threshold).

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in NH (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets NH economic nexus threshold ($109,000 gross income)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - BPT filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
NH BPT filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in NH if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in NH - Employees or agents working in NH - Tangible personal property located in NH - Real property located in NH
Reference: RSA 77-A:1 (Business Profits Tax definitions and nexus) Reference: NH Rev 300.01 (Nexus standards) Reference: NH DRA Business Profits Tax FAQ (Nexus requirements)

NH BPT filing required due to economic nexus.
Economic nexus threshold: $109,000 gross business income from all activities. (Threshold adjusted biennially; $109,000 for periods beginning on or after 1/1/2025)
NH does NOT have a transaction count threshold - only gross receipts.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), NH requires BPT filing if gross business income exceeds the threshold, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: RSA 77-A:1 (Filing thresholds) Reference: NH Rev 300.02 (Economic nexus provisions) Reference: NH DRA Business Enterprise Tax and Business Profits Tax Filing Threshold Adjustment

No NH nexus or below filing threshold - no BPT filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Gross business income must exceed $109,000 (2025) to require filing. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: RSA 77-A:1 (Filing requirements) Reference: NH Rev 300.02 (Nexus and filing threshold)

decision_table.name: Calculate_NH_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate NH state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income. NH uses static conformity to IRC as of December 31, 2018, and has decoupled from Section 163(j) interest limitations.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
NH state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
NH ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to NH) - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Deductions for federal provisions enacted after December 31, 2018 (static conformity) - Certain expenses related to exempt income
NH SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on NH state and municipal bonds - Business interest expense disallowed under Section 163(j) (NH allows full deduction effective 1/1/2024 per Senate Bill 189 signed 7/28/2023) - Carryforward of Section 163(j) interest from pre-2024 years (deductible over 3 years) - Dividends received deduction (if applicable) - NH net operating loss deduction (subject to NH limitations)
CRITICAL: NH uses static conformity to the IRC as of December 31, 2018. Federal tax law changes after that date do NOT automatically apply to NH BPT unless specifically adopted by NH legislation.
CRITICAL: NH decoupled from Section 163(j) business interest limitation. Interest disallowed for federal purposes under Section 163(j) is FULLY DEDUCTIBLE for NH BPT purposes (effective for tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2024).
Reference: RSA 77-A:1 (Definitions - "Gross business profits") Reference: Senate Bill 189 (2023) - Section 163(j) decoupling Reference: NH Rev 300.03 (Additions to federal taxable income) Reference: NH Rev 300.04 (Subtractions from federal taxable income) Reference: NH Form BT-Summary Instructions (Additions and Subtractions schedules)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have NH nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_NH_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate NH Business Profits Tax (BPT). Applies NH 7.5% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted business profits.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
NH Business Profits Tax (BPT) calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to NH: × [NH apportionment percentage (single-sales)] 3. NH additions: + [Federal interest, state taxes, post-2018 provisions] 4. NH subtractions: - [NH municipal interest, Section 163(j) interest, dividends] 5. NH taxable business profits: = [Result] 6. NH BPT rate: × 7.5% (flat rate) 7. NH Business Profits Tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. NH credits: - [R&D, Coos County jobs, Economic Revitalization Zone, BET credit] 9. NH BPT liability: = [Final tax]
NH uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
NH BPT rate history: - 2025+: 7.5% (for tax periods ending on or after 12/31/2023) - Previous years: Higher rates (gradually reduced over time)
NH provides various tax credits including: - Research & Development Credit (RSA 77-A:5-b) - Coos County Job Creation Credit (RSA 77-A:5-c) - Economic Revitalization Zone Credit (RSA 162-N) - Business Enterprise Tax (BET) credit against BPT (RSA 77-E:3-a)
IMPORTANT: BET is a separate tax on enterprise value base (compensation, interest, dividends). BET paid may be credited against BPT to prevent double taxation. BET is not implemented in this decision table.
Reference: RSA 77-A:2 (BPT rate of 7.5%) Reference: RSA 77-A:3 (Apportionment - single-sales factor) Reference: RSA 77-A:5 (Tax credits) Reference: NH Form BT-Summary (Business Tax Return) Reference: NH Rev 300 (Business Profits Tax regulations)

No NH nexus or below filing threshold - no BPT liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in NH, or gross business income is below $109,000 filing threshold (2025). Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: RSA 77-A:1 (Filing requirements and nexus)

No NH taxable business profits - no BPT liability.
Corporation has NH nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
NH net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - NH allows NOL carryforward (subject to limitations) - NOL carryback provisions vary by tax year - NH NOL rules may differ from federal due to static conformity to IRC as of December 31, 2018
Reference: RSA 77-A:4 (Net operating loss deduction) Reference: NH Form BT-Summary Instructions (NOL schedules)
